messages:
Renee: heads up — trying to use the JS SDK from a Next middleware and hitting a weird build error on Vercel: `Module not found: Can't resolve 'fs'` even though middleware is edge. anyone seen this? :confused:

Carlos: yup. this usually means the bundler picked up the CJS/node entry for the package. Next's resolver and some builders will resolve conditionally but can pick the wrong target if package.json exports are ambiguous.

Tara: small repro: creating `middleware.ts` that does `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'` and then calling client inside the middleware. local dev (vite) works, vercel build fails.

Carlos: quick workarounds while we ship a proper edge build:
- keep imports inside the handler (lazy import)
- dynamic import the edge bundle path: `const { createClient } = await import('@redwood/sdk/dist/edge.mjs')`
- or use a pinned dist-tag that contains an edge-only entry if we publish one

Renee: lazy import fixed my deploy for now. curious — is there a way to make TS not complain about `Request` differences in edge? I get `Property 'json' does not exist on type 'Request'`.

Tara: TS picks up lib defs from tsconfig. For Next edge middleware set tsconfig lib to include dom and es2021. Example:
```json
{
  "compilerOptions": {
    "lib": ["es2021", "dom"],
    "types": ["@types/node"] // careful: node types can conflict — remove for edge files
  }
}
```
Better: create a `types/edge.d.ts` and augment the global Request interface just for edge build, or scope the `types` to server-only configs.

Carlos: FYI we're prototyping a proper package layout to avoid this: add an explicit `/edge` export subpath in package.json and ship a tiny ESM-only bundle that imports zero node deps. Example exports snippet:
```json
"exports": {
  "./edge": "./dist/edge/index.mjs",
  "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
  "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
}
```
We also plan to add `typesVersions` so TS can resolve different .d.ts files for edge vs node consumers.

Renee: will that also help bundlers (rspack/esbuild) not shim node builtins?

Carlos: yep — if bundlers resolve `@redwood/sdk/edge` they'll never see `fs` or `stream` imports. The tricky part is consumers using the root import — bundlers sometimes pre-resolve package.json conditions and still pick wrong entry. That's why we recommend explicit `/edge` import in middleware for now.

Tara: additional gotcha: some transitive deps import `stream` at top-level (e.g., telemetry libs). Even if not used, bundlers can include shims or error. We audited deps and replaced a small telemetry helper with a no-op for edge builds.

Renee: any Next-specific config flags to watch?

Carlos: a few notes:
- Name file `middleware.ts` so Next treats it as edge (older Next versions differ).
- `experimental.esmExternals` and `experimental.rsc` flags can change resolver behavior — test both if you're blocked.
- For Vercel, check the build logs to see which builder/bundler was used — it sometimes overrides local bundler assumptions.

Tara: also adding a short DX doc and an example repo showing correct tsconfig + next.config + middleware import patterns. Will include the lazy/dynamic import snippets and a checklist for onboarding teams.

ci-bot: opened issue #623 in redwood-js-sdk: "Edge entrypoint + TS resolver guidance for Next middleware" — https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-js-sdk/issues/623 :rocket:

vercel-bot: Build log hint: Vercel used @vercel/next builder with esbuild; unresolved module: 'fs' referenced from /node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/cjs/index.js

Renee: thanks all — I'll switch to the dynamic edge import and add a note in the project onboarding doc. please ping when the /edge export goes out so we can switch to a stable import. :pray:
